title: Not All Forests Are Equal: Mapping the World’s Forests
gist: Google DeepMind, Google Research, WRI and IIASA released ForTy 2020, a free 10-meter global map classifying land into six forest and land-use types plus a 2017-2025 annual time series, built to support EU deforestation regulation compliance and reporting 90% accuracy on forest type.

insights.claim: Google DeepMind and Google Research with WRI and IIASA released Forest Typology (ForTy) 2020, classifying every 10-by-10-meter patch of land into primary, naturally regenerating, planted, plantation, tree crop/agroforestry, or other land, openly licensed on Google Earth Engine.
insights.speaker: Maxim Neumann and Charlotte Stanton
insights.so_what: Free high-resolution forest-type data lowers the cost of deforestation-risk screening for supply chains.
insights.locator: Today, Google DeepMind and Google Research

insights.claim: ForTy picked the correct forest type 90% of the time and separated forest from non-forest 95% of the time against more than 9,000 randomly chosen, expert-verified sites, outperforming other global forest maps.
insights.speaker: Maxim Neumann and Charlotte Stanton
insights.so_what: Validated accuracy supports use in compliance, though 10% type error leaves residual risk.
insights.locator: Putting the map to the test

insights.claim: The model was trained on about 1.7 million labeled locations and uses AlphaEarth Foundations embeddings to detect planting patterns, growth cycles and harvest rhythms, and it outputs per-class probabilities rather than hard labels.
insights.speaker: Maxim Neumann and Charlotte Stanton
insights.so_what: Probability outputs let users tune thresholds, for example strict cutoffs for regulatory risk.
insights.locator: Training our ForTy model was challenging

insights.claim: The EU Deforestation Regulation requires that coffee, cocoa and palm oil not come from land that was forest in 2020 and was later converted to agriculture, and that wood products not come from primary or regenerating forest converted to plantations.
insights.speaker: Maxim Neumann and Charlotte Stanton
insights.so_what: Commodity importers into the EU need forest-type, not just tree-cover, evidence of land history.

insights.claim: Standard tree-cover maps can miss natural forest logged and replanted as plantation because the land looks green again, which ForTy's 2017–2025 time series is designed to reveal.
insights.speaker: Maxim Neumann and Charlotte Stanton
insights.so_what: Conversion to plantation can hide from legacy satellite monitoring, so supply-chain claims based on tree cover may understate deforestation.
insights.locator: This differentiation matters because some of the most important changes

insights.claim: A primary forest that has never been cleared holds far more carbon and biodiversity than a single-species timber plantation harvested every decade or two, so forest type matters for carbon accounting and conservation finance.
insights.speaker: Maxim Neumann and Charlotte Stanton
insights.so_what: Carbon-credit and forest-finance valuation depends on distinguishing natural from planted forest.
insights.locator: But a forest’s ecological value also depends on its history
